title: Home life
hookLine: someone asked 'A'ishah what he did at home; she said he served his family, and when the prayer came, he went to pray

lines: WHAT DID HE DO AT HOME?
ASK THE ONE WHO LIVED WITH HIM.
cards: A question put to 'A'ishah, and kept in Sahih al-Bukhari. Someone asked her what the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, used to do in his house. Not in the mosque.
Not on the battlefield, not on the pulpit. In the house. It's the kind of thing you'd only ask the person who lived with him.
Her answer is short. He used to be busy serving his family, she said, and when the time for prayer came, he went out to the prayer. No speech.
A man at home doing the work of the home, until the call came.

teach.h: FIRST THE FAMILY, THEN THE PRAYER.
teach.b: Look at the order in her answer: first the family, then the prayer. Not because the prayer mattered less. When its time came, he went, and the serving stopped.
But until then, the house had his hands.

teach.h: MIHNAH, THE WORK OF THE HOUSE.
teach.b: The word in the Arabic report is mihnah, the work of the household, the everyday labor of a home. Other reports fill in the picture.
In one kept in the Musnad of Ahmad, 'A'ishah is asked again, and she says, in paraphrase, that he mended his own clothes, repaired his own sandal, and did what any man does in his house.

A man the Qur'an calls a messenger, sewing a torn garment himself. Now put that next to yesterday's hadith: the best of you are the best to their families. The serving is what that sentence looks like on a Tuesday.
A shirt. A sandal strap. Whatever needs doing.
And the second half of her answer keeps the serving from swallowing everything.

teach.h: THE HOUSE AND THE PRAYER TAKE TURNS.
teach.b: The home was not a reason to miss the prayer, and the prayer was not a reason to skip the home. Some readers hear in this a rhythm for a whole life: the small work of love, then the turn toward Allah, then back again.
The house and the prayer aren't rivals. They take turns. The prayer, when he left for it, was not an escape from the dishes.
It was the next thing in the same day.

how: Muslims point to 'A'ishah's description of the Prophet at home, serving his family and mending his own clothes, as a model for household life, and to his going out when the time for prayer came.

o: serving the family at home, and going out when prayer came
leaving the housework to others so prayer comes first
keeping home and worship apart, so neither disturbs the other

p: what did he do in his house?

s: in 'A'ishah's answer, he left the housework to others
she said he used to be busy serving his family.
a report says he mended his own clothes and sandal
it's kept in the Musnad of Ahmad, from 'A'ishah.
in her answer, the housework kept him from the prayer
when the time for prayer came, he went out to pray.

games.q: you're asked what the Prophet did at home. you lived with him. what do you say?
o: he spent the whole time in worship.
he served his family, and went out when prayer came.
he rested from the work outside.
games.why: 'A'ishah's answer in al-Bukhari: he served his family, and when prayer came he went to pray.

practice: Let your mind walk through the place you live: the sink, the laundry, the thing that's been broken for a week.
Pick one small job you'd normally leave for someone else, and see yourself doing it start to finish, without telling anyone.
Then see yourself turning toward the next thing in your day; if you pray, let that be the next prayer, whenever its time comes.

wordCard.voice: Home life. In 'A'ishah's answer: he served his family, mended his clothes, and when prayer came, went to pray. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: work, the household labor in 'A'ishah's answer.

carryVoice: Your line: serve, then pray. A sandal strap, and then the call. Rest well.
